## Exact model and all-size proof

The separated-generator chart is S_ij=a_i b_j for i>j, S_ii=d_i, and S_ij=c_i e_j for i<j. It is not the entire exceptional/singular quasiseparable-order-one variety. Products have t stages with fixed intermediate permutations, in complex Zariski closure.

There are 2N−2 active lower coordinates and one free scalar redundancy on the nonzero open chart, giving dimension 2N−3. The upper triangle contributes the same independently; the diagonal contributes N. Hence dim V_N=5N−6. Invertible stages form a nonempty dense open subset because diagonal invertible matrices belong to the chart. Each of the t−1 boundaries admits an N-dimensional diagonal gauge. Its action on an invertible tuple is free, recursively from the first stage. Therefore product-image dimension is at most t(5N−6)−(t−1)N=N+t(4N−6), capped by N². Density extends this upper bound to the full image closure. A finite union over permutations has the same maximum bound. The generic required depth is ceil((N²−N)/(4N−6)), equal to N/4+1 when 4|N≥4.

For identity shuffles, an off-diagonal cut block of AB is the sum of two products whose ranks are bounded by the corresponding cut ranks of A and B. Thus quasiseparable orders add, and identity-shuffle t-stage products have order at most t. This is a generic-matrix obstruction, not a Fourier-specific one.
